newsitem.title: USA: U.S. experts raise GDP forecast in Blue Chip poll.
newsitem.headline: U.S. experts raise GDP forecast in Blue Chip poll.

text.p: Experts in a closely watched economic survey have bumped up their forecasts for 1997 U.S. gross domestic product growth after the brisk pace of activity recorded in the final quarter of last year.
The Blue Chip Economic Indicators consensus forecast for economic growth this year rose to 2.5 percent from 2.3 percent in the last poll in January.
Growth of 2.5 percent would put this year on a par with 1996. The fourth quarter of last year was particularly strong, as the economy grew by 4.7 percent.

While raising their forecasts for overall growth, economists in the Blue Chip poll also boosted their forecasts for inflation. The analysts predicted a rise of 3.0 percent in the Consumer Price Index this year, up from the previous forecast of 2.9 percent.
Despite a slightly less optimistic inflation outlook, the economists are still betting that the Federal Reserve will refrain from raising interest rates.

"While officials at the Federal Reserve continue to hint they are inching closer to a tightening of monetary policy, the consensus remains unconvinced that the Fed will act to hike rates this year," a summary of the latest Blue Chip poll said.
